ai.title: Add Claude fallback notification tag
ai.summary: Yields `<codebuff_claude_fallback_info>` when all Gemini API attempts fail and execution falls back to Claude Sonnet. Replaces hardcoded string checks with `ONE_TIME_TAGS` constants in `common/src/constants.ts` to standardize rate-limit and fallback notifications. Updates `backend/src/llm-apis/gemini-with-fallbacks.ts` to use `GoogleGenerativeAIError` for 429 detection and `npm-app/src/client.ts` to manage one-time display state via a generic tag map.

eli5.text: When the assistant's main AI model can't answer your question because it's overloaded, you'll now see a clear message saying it's switching to a backup AI instead of silently changing tools. The message appears once per conversation and looks like a small notice in brackets. This only happens when you use the default AI model and it hits its rate limit.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.206
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.206 in npm-app/package.json. Release increment for codebuff. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The latest update keeps the assistant's terminal commands showing exactly what you meant, even when they contain special characters like ampersands. Previously, codes such as & in a command could appear literally in the terminal instead of running as the intended symbol &, which could break commands you asked the assistant to execute. The update also makes the assistant tell you in plain notice when it has to switch to a backup provider because your primary one was unavailable, so you are not left guessing why a response changed tone or source. These changes are live today.

ai.title: Add invalid API key handling and cost tracking for user keys
ai.summary: Gemini fallback logic detects API_KEY_INVALID errors to yield user-specific warnings via new CODEBUFF_INVALID_KEY_INFO constant. Message cost tracker now accepts usesUserApiKey flag to adjust credit calculation based on key ownership. Stream processors trim chunks before tag detection to prevent whitespace issues in client display.

eli5.text: When you supply your own Gemini API key to the assistant and that key is rejected, the system now notices the specific "invalid key" error and tells you with a clear, one-time warning message instead of silently retrying other keys or showing a generic failure. Your own usage and costs are also tracked separately from the shared pool when you use your personal key, so the credit math no longer charges the normal service margin to your own key's consumption. These warnings and cost adjustments are live today for anyone who connects their own Gemini key, and you would see a short yellow notice appear in your terminal the first time an invalid key is detected.

ai.title: npm-app version bump to 1.0.207
ai.summary: Version in npm-app/package.json bumped from 1.0.206 to 1.0.207. Scope limited to package metadata.

eli5.text: The assistant's product name version number ticked up to a new release, which bundles in handling for invalid API keys, when your key is rejected, you now get a clear, specific warning instead of a generic failure, and your own usage costs are tracked separately. If you updated today, you'd see that new warning behavior plus a small tag noting when a backup AI provider steps in to keep your request moving.

ai.title: Add XML attribute warning to file edit tool prompt
ai.summary: Added a warning in `backend/src/tools.ts` instructing the agent not to use XML attributes (e.g., `<path name="foo">`) as they break the tool. Removed unused `logger` import. This change affects the system prompt for the file editing tool.

eli5.text: When you use the file-editing tool, its instructions now warn you not to write things like `<path name="foo">` because doing so silently breaks the edit. The reminder shows up in the help text you see before editing, and the unused logging code that supported it was removed at the same time.

ai.title: Fix last-line deletion when tool calls end turn
ai.summary: Added `end_turn` check to console newline logic in `npm-app/src/client.ts`. Last line sometimes deleted when tool calls ended turn without returning results. Ensures proper spacing by emitting newline if `end_turn` is present.

eli5.text: When an assistant finishes a turn by ending it without showing results, the last line of the previous message was sometimes getting deleted by accident. The system now checks specifically for this end-of-turn situation and makes sure there's a line break in the right place to keep the last line visible. You'd notice the difference if you were reading a conversation where the assistant wraps things up abruptly without returning any output - the previous message's final line would stay intact instead of disappearing. This fix is live today for anyone using the tool.

ai.title: CLI crash guards and tool call error handling
ai.summary: Added process-level handlers for `unhandledRejection` and `uncaughtException` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to prevent silent CLI crashes. Wrapped tool call execution logic in `npm-app/src/client.ts` with `try/catch` blocks to catch and display errors from `handleToolCall` without terminating the session. Changes are internal to the CLI package.

eli5.text: The command-line tool now keeps running when it hits an unexpected error instead of silently quitting. If a tool call fails or something goes wrong mid-session, the tool catches the error, shows you a message, and brings you back to a fresh prompt rather than ending your session. This affects anyone using the CLI package today, and the tool remains live and usable afterward.

ai.title: Update April 2025 Hackathon details
ai.summary: Adjusts event schedule to April 12th, 2:00 PM - 8:00 PM PDT. Adds judges section listing James Grugett, Charles Lien, and Cher Hu. Updates copy to emphasize free dinner and Codebuff credits.

eli5.text: Visitors to the Codebuff hackathon website will now see the event is scheduled for Sunday, April 12th, from 2:00 PM to 8:00 PM PDT, rather than the previously listed April 13th and 11:00 AM start time. The page also introduces a new section naming the three judges overseeing the competition, James Grugett, Charles Lien, and Cher Hu, and tweaks the event description to highlight that a catered dinner and free Codebuff credits are provided. The event is live on the website today and applies to anyone planning to attend or follow along.
